mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or Business Registration Certificate of each foreign shareholder and ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or corporate registrar in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive alternative: if the issuing jurisdiction is party to the Hague Apostille Convention, sequence is (i) local notarization, (ii) Apostille issued by the designated Competent Authority, (iii) no PRC consular legalization. If the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille member, sequence is (i) local notarization, (ii) authentication by the issuing country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs or registry, (iii) legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China, (iv) no Apostille. Never chain Apostille and consular legalization in the same document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The mandatory screening protocol requires verification of every beneficial owner, director, legal representative, supervisor, and authorized signatory against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK HM Treasury sanctions, China's terrorist financing list, PBOC administrative penalty databases, SAMR registration disqualification records, and INTERPOL notices. Enhanced due diligence must be applied to politically exposed persons (PEPs), family members, and close associates; the firm must document source of wealth, source of funds, business rationale, and adverse media. Positive hits must be escalated before any incorporation filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Self-Declaration System, accessed through provincial SAMR online service portals under the National Integrated Government Service Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A WFOE legal name must be in Simplified Chinese characters and follow the mandatory four-tier format: administrative division plus distinctive name plus industry description plus organizational form. The foreign investor's transliterated brand name may be used as the distinctive name if phonetically converted into Chinese characters. No stand-alone foreign-language name is accepted for the Chinese legal name, although a parallel English name may be used for banking and seal purposes. Latin letters and Arabic numerals are generally prohibited in the Chinese legal name unless specifically approved by the competent market regulator. The proposed name must be distinguishable from all registered names nationwide; identical or near-identical names are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days of receiving the written rejection notice, the applicant may resubmit a corrected name through the SAMR name declaration system. If the rejection is based on a formal legal decision, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the next higher market regulation authority or the same-level people's government within 60 days. The appeal package must include the reconsideration application, the original rejection notice, identity certificates, the proposed name and structure rationale, and evidence of distinctiveness. The reconsideration authority must decide within 60 days, extendable once by 30 days. If the administrative reconsideration remains adverse, the applicant may initiate an administrative lawsuit within 6 months before the competent Intermediate People's Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered address for a WFOE engaged in ISIC 4390 deep slurry trenching and continuous cut-off wall works. The PRC Company Law requires a genuine physical registered address and the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development construction qualification rules require an operational office, technical personnel, performance capability, and project oversight facilities. Municipal tax authorities and banks reject virtual-only arrangements for this industry because general taxpayer inspection, official tax invoice control, and physical on-site verification require an actual place of business. A virtual office may be used only as a supplementary liaison and mail collection point after a fully compliant physical registered office is established, never as the primary address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical inspection by municipal tax or registry authorities is approximately 75 to 85 percent within the first 12 months if the company relies on a shared, virtual, or non-operational address; the risk drops to approximately 20 to 30 percent if a fully physical office with permanent staff, lease, signboard, books, and site-management capability is maintained. Checklist for inspection readiness: (1) original lease agreement and landlord identity and ownership documents; (2) legible company signboard at the registered address; (3) key personnel present during normal business hours; (4) statutory corporate records, seal-use logs, accounting ledgers, and bank confirmation; (5) official tax invoice controls and tax filings; (6) construction qualification certificate, safety permits, and project contracts; (7) registration of each diaphragm wall project site office; and (8) insurance and employment records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), Articles 22 to 98 governing limited liability companies; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 11 and 12; Regulations for Implementing the Foreign Investment Law (2019), Articles 10 to 13; Administration of Market Registration Regulations (2021 Revision), Articles 8 to 25.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Administration for Market Regulation at the district, city or provincial level where the WFOE's registered office is located, with the integrated foreign investment information report transmitted automatically to the Ministry of Commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, submitted together with the Articles of Association, the Foreign Investment Information Report, and supporting corporate documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: China's Company Law (2023 Revision) imposes no universal minimum paid-up capital for a limited liability company. Registered capital is subscribed under the Articles of Association and must be fully paid in within five years after establishment, unless an applicable industry regulation requires a shorter contribution period. For a construction contractor holding a foundation specialty qualification under ISIC 4390, the competent construction authority may require paid-in capital sufficient to meet the qualification class and contractual liability thresholds. No blocked escrow account is imposed by the corporate registry for ordinary WFOE incorporation; however, foreign exchange controls require the foreign investor to remit contributions to a dedicated foreign-invested enterprise capital settlement account opened with a licensed Chinese bank and supervised by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, unanimously and without dissent, that the establishment of CN WFOE LTD as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company under the laws of the People's Republic of China is hereby ratified, and the share capital subscription plan set forth in the Articles of Association is approved in its entirety; the sole member and subscriber hereby subscribes in full to the registered capital of the company at the value and contribution schedule stated in the Articles, with each share conferring one vote, and the board is instructed to open and maintain mandatory capital contribution accounts in accordance with the Foreign Investment Information Report requirements and the rules of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange for foreign settlement of capital in RMB or foreign currency. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the company shall be the physical address specified in the establishment application and the lease agreement submitted to the Administration for Market Regulation, and management is authorised to execute the office lease, pay all registration fees, and attend to the statutory filing of the registered address with the local market supervision authority. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following statutory officers be and are hereby appointed: one executive director and legal representative, one supervisor who is not an officer or employee of the company, one general manager, and one chief finance officer, each of whom shall serve until removal by the sole member in accordance with the Articles of Association; the general manager is authorised to open bank settlement accounts, foreign exchange capital accounts, and qualified business accounts at licensed banks in the People's Republic of China, and to designate dual signatories comprising the legal representative and the chief finance officer for all cheque, wire and electronic payment instruments. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the company shall adopt a company seal, finance seal, invoice seal and legal representative name seal, and that the responsible officers shall register those seals with the public security unit and the taxation authority. RESOLVED FURTHER, that management is directed to obtain the construction enterprise qualification, safe production certificate, environmental impact registrations, civil defence fire safety approvals and all other industrial licences required for deep slurry trenching and underground continuous cut-off wall works, and further directed to file the foreign investment information report, complete social insurance and tax registrations, and execute the step-by-step formation protocol set out in the formation dossier. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all officers are authorised to sign, notarise, legalise and submit such declarations, bank mandates, powers of attorney, certificates and affidavits as may be required to perfect these resolutions, and that this resolution shall continue in full force and effect until amended or revoked by the sole member.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Foreign Investment Negative List Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Name Registration Online Service, administered locally by the municipal or district Administration for Market Regulation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the national enterprise registration portal and conduct a name search to verify that the proposed legal name of CN WFOE LTD does not conflict with existing registered enterprise names or protected trademarks and does not contain prohibited wording. Prepare at least three alternative names in Chinese-language transliteration and in English. Submit the name pre-approval application online together with a letter from the foreign investor and a preliminary business scope classification under ISIC 4390. The registry system will screen against the Foreign Investment Negative List; if the proposed scope is not restricted or prohibited, the system issues an electronic name notice. Once granted, the name is reserved for six months, during which the formal establishment application must be filed.
required_dossiers: Duly completed enterprise name registration application form
Foreign investor's letter of intent and certificate of incorporation or identity documentation
Power of attorney appointing the local formation agent
Translator's accuracy certificate for all foreign-language documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict, file a fresh application with an alternate name within two working days. If the negative-list screening returns a restriction, revise the business scope to exclude the prohibited element or apply for the required foreign investment approval before resubmitting the name application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Articles of Association and Filing of Establishment Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation at the district, municipal or provincial level where the registered office is situated, through the integrated online registration portal or physical service hall.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Articles of Association, capital contribution schedule and the foreign investment information report. Authenticate or legalise the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation through consular legalisation or apostille, and arrange certified Chinese-language translation of all offshore documents. Submit the formation application online or at the AMR service hall. The registry will review the documents for legal validity, verify the legal representative's identity, check the registered address lease and underlying title documents, and confirm that the business scope is not on the prohibited list. Upon approval, the AMR issues the unified business license with the unified social credit code. The foreign investment information report is generated from the same filing and transmitted electronically to the Ministry of Commerce, so no separate approval is required for a business outside the foreign investment negative list.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association signed by all subscribers
Application form for establishment registration of a foreign-invested limited liability company
Notarised and legalised certificate of incorporation of the foreign investor, with certified Chinese translation
Bank reference letter or other evidence of financial standing of the foreign investor
Registered office lease agreement or ownership certificate and landlord identification documents
Appointment documents for the executive director, supervisor, general manager and legal representative
Identity documents and photographs of the legal representative, supervisor and managers
Name pre-approval notice issued by SAMR
Foreign investment information report prepared in the required electronic format
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMR issues a correction notice, rectify all incomplete items and resubmit within the statutory fifteen-day correction period. If the application is suspended on grounds of deficient notarisation or legalisation, re-legalise the foreign documents and apply for administrative reconsideration within sixty days of the suspension notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Seal Carving, Bank Account Opening and Capital Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau (PSB) designated seal engraving service for official seals; licensed commercial bank branch for foreign-invested enterprise settlement accounts; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) acting through the bank's foreign exchange business window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the business license, apply to an approved seal engraving house to produce the company seal, finance seal, invoice seal and legal representative name seal. File the seal registration particulars with the public security organ. Thereafter open a bank settlement account and a foreign capital settlement account at a licensed Chinese bank, presenting the original business license, seals, board resolutions and identity documents of the legal representative and finance officer. The bank acts as the designated reporting institution for SAFE. The foreign investor shall then remit the subscribed capital within the contribution period fixed in the Articles of Association, not exceeding five years from establishment. Each inward remittance must be reported under the foreign-invested enterprise capital code and credited to the capital settlement account. The bank will permit conversion to RMB after verifying the authenticity and intended use of the funds.
required_dossiers: Original business license and unified social credit code certificate
Public Security Bureau approval or seal registration certificate
Articles of Association and any shareholder resolutions
Appointment record for the legal representative and chief finance officer
Company seal, finance seal, invoice seal and legal representative name seal
Bank account opening application forms and standard bank mandate agreements
Foreign investment information report filing receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines to open the foreign capital settlement account due to incomplete beneficial ownership information, provide the requested ultimate beneficial owner declaration and enhanced due diligence pack. If SAFE flags the remittance code, submit a written supplemental explanation and seek reclassification of the transaction before repeating the transfer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Invoice Application and Social Insurance and Statistical Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration local tax office through the integrated online tax portal; National Social Insurance Administration portal; National Bureau of Statistics via the local statistics bureau.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete tax registration within thirty days after issuance of the business license. The tax authority will record the company's taxpayer status, tax categories, accounting standards and filing cycles. Apply for value-added tax general taxpayer status if expected annual turnover exceeds the statutory threshold, and apply for an electronic invoice booklet and invoice approval for construction services. Register social insurance for employees, housing fund obligations and statistical reporting duties. Because the company is engaged in physical construction works, also establish the project-specific wage payment platform for construction workers. The tax authority will link the company's bank account number to the electronic filing record, enabling automated tax payments and monthly or quarterly returns.
required_dossiers: Business license and unified social credit code certificate
Bank account opening certificate or bank confirmation letter
Identity documents of the legal representative and chief finance officer
Articles of Association and registered office proof
Tax registration statement and social insurance registration forms
Seal imprint specimens for the company seal and finance seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is suspended for missing payroll or accounting systems, provide the required corporate accounting manual and system accession evidence. If penalty notices are issued for delayed filing, pay the penalty and request waiver under the Tax Administration Law. A written objection may be lodged with the local tax office within sixty days of any adverse assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Construction Enterprise Qualification and Safe Production Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Department of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD), administered by the local Housing and Urban-Rural Construction Commission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the registered business scope covers deep slurry trenching and underground continuous cut-off wall works under ISIC 4390, the WFOE must obtain a Construction Enterprise Qualification Certificate corresponding to foundation and foundation treatment specialty contracting. Prepare the corporate profile, verified registered capital evidence, technical equipment ownership or lease documents, and the list of certified registered constructors, engineers, safety officers and key technical personnel. Submit the application through the provincial construction administration portal. The authority will verify personnel qualifications, audit financial capacity and may conduct a field review of the internal management system. After the qualification certificate is granted, apply separately for the Safety Production Certificate for construction enterprises. Temporary site licences must be filed with the municipal construction commission before commencing each physical project.
required_dossiers: Business license and unified social credit code certificate
Registered capital contribution certificate and bank statement
Technical equipment inventory with ownership or lease certificates
Employment contracts and professional qualifications of registered constructors, engineers and technicians
Safety production responsibility system, safety rules and emergency response plans
Social insurance payment certificates for technical staff members
Performance records of similar deep foundation, slurry wall or ground improvement works if required by the qualification class
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the qualification application is rejected for insuffficiency of technical personnel or equipment, use the statutory correction period to replace certificates and reapply. If the authority questions the proportion of foreign technical personnel, submit evidence of qualified Chinese staff employment. An administrative reconsideration may be filed within sixty days of the rejection, and an administrative lawsuit within six months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Impact Registration, Civil Defence Fire Permit and Site-Specific Operational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau; local fire rescue unit under the Ministry of Emergency Management or MOHURD; local Emergency Management Bureau for workplace safety.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Since the WFOE operates physical construction equipment, slurry treatment facilities and field support yards, the company must determine its environmental filing duty. A contractor's equipment maintenance yard ordinarily requires only an environmental impact registration table if pollution is minor. For each construction project, the project owner normally holds the environmental impact assessment approval, but the WFOE must verify that its slurry trenching, cement bentonite mixing, spoil disposal and diesel operations comply with the approved mitigation measures. Install sedimentation tanks, oil-water separators and hazardous waste storage areas. Apply for civil defence fire inspection certificates for temporary site offices and sheds. Register mobile cranes, slurry pumps and pressure vessels under the special equipment safety supervision system. Conduct confined space and deep excavation safety assessments with rescue planning before operating.
required_dossiers: Environmental impact registration form or project EIA approval report
Pollutant discharge permit or relevant exemption letter
Wastewater and hazardous waste management protocols
Fire safety design review and acceptance certificates for temporary structures and site facilities
Safety Production Certificate for construction enterprises
Special equipment use registration certificates for cranes, pressure vessels and hoisting equipment
Emergency response plan, training records and exercise reports
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ecology and Environment Bureau upgrades the filing to a full environmental impact report, prepare supplemental ambient monitoring data and seek a scoping opinion to narrow the review. If fire safety inspection identifies deficiencies, correct the listed items and request re-inspection. Continued non-compliance will result in suspension of site operations until the relevant permits are restored.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD) and the provincial Housing and Urban-Rural Construction Commission; local Emergency Management Bureau and Market Supervision Administration for construction and site safety permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Construction Enterprise Qualification Certificate for Foundation and Foundation Treatment Specialty Contracting; Safety Production Permit for Construction Enterprises; Temporary Civil Defence Fire Safety Inspection Certificate for each physical construction site.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China and the local Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-level Full EIA Report is prepared by the construction project owner; the WFOE as a specialty contractor is subject to Category C Environmental Impact Registration for its equipment maintenance yard and field support facilities. If the site includes slurry recycling ponds, hazardous waste storage or fuel storage exceeding classification thresholds, a Class B EIA Report may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from slurry treatment and equipment washing must pass through settlement basins to achieve suspended solids below 70 mg/L, pH between 6 and 9, and total petroleum hydrocarbons below 5 mg/L before discharge to municipal networks. Volatile organic compounds from diesel equipment must be limited by using ultra-low-sulphur fuel, routine maintenance and controlled engine idling. Hazardous wastes, including waste oil, spent batteries and paint residues, must be stored in sealed labelled containers on impermeable floors and transferred to licensed hazardous waste treatment units within the statutory storage period. Slurry spoil may only be disposed at approved dredged material or construction waste sites.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defence Fire Safety Inspection Certificate for temporary site offices, sheds, welding areas and storage compounds; structural verification of diaphragm wall guide walls, deep excavation support systems and access roads; occupational health and safety pre-start review under the Law on Work Safety; special equipment registration certificates for cranes, slurry pumps and pressure vessels; safe work permits for confined space entry, deep excavation and underground operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) via the electronic tax portal 'E-Tax Bureau' (e-Tax electronic tax office) available at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn for entity registration and ongoing compliance filings
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) in China must first obtain the Foreign Investment Business License and other statutory licenses from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), then complete tax registration within 30 days of the business license issuance. The WFOE must submit the original business license, articles of association, incorporation documents, foreign investment information report, legal representative identity documents, and lease or ownership proof for the registered business premises to the local competent tax authority. The tax authority issues a unique Tax Identification Number (TIN) in the format of the unified social credit code (18-digit USCC) which serves as the taxpayer identification number, plus a separate taxpayer registration certificate if required. Tax registration may be completed online through the E-Tax Bureau portal by logging in with the enterprise electronic certificate (e-tax certificate USB key or digital CA certificate), filing the 'Tax Registration Form for Enterprises', and uploading the required scanned documents. After approval, the entity is assigned one or more tax identifiers for enterprise income tax, value-added tax, municipal construction tax, education surcharges, stamp duty, and other applicable taxes. The WFOE should also register for foreign exchange administration and open a RMB and foreign currency bank account with a designated domestic bank, and the banking and foreign exchange registration need not be completed before tax registration but must be coordinated for operational continuity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China does not provide a check-the-box classification regime comparable to the United States. The WFOE is automatically classified as a resident enterprise taxed at entity level under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. No hybrid mismatch election is available to a WFOE under domestic law; however, the entity may apply treaty eligibility for reduced withholding rates under an applicable double tax agreement and must document beneficial ownership. The only statutory elections relevant include the choice of foreign currency accounting if approved by the tax authority, the simplified VAT computation method for certain eligible construction services where the taxpayer elects the deemed deduction method (simplified method) for VAT on construction services, and the annual election for allocation of common expenses under transfer pricing documentation rules, but these are not entity classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration applies to all entities and individuals whose taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000 per 12-month rolling period for general taxpayer status. Small-scale taxpayers with taxable annual sales below RMB 5,000,000 may register voluntarily but are not obligated to register as general taxpayers unless their turnover exceeds the threshold. Foreign enterprises engaged in construction services within China must register for VAT regardless of the threshold if they perform taxable services in China, and they may appoint a domestic withholding agent if they do not have a permanent establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a mandatory electronic invoice system integrated with the STA's VAT invoice system. General VAT taxpayers must use the official UKey or tax-control equipment to issue fully digital electronic invoices ('fully digitalized electronic invoices' with a 20-digit invoice number) through the E-Tax Bureau platform. Invoices are transmitted in real time to the national VAT invoice service platform and subject to automated anti-fraud verification via tax control codes, digital signatures, and the national electronic invoice monitoring system. Since April 2025, the STA is expanding full digital invoice pilots nationwide; all invoices issued by registered enterprises must include the statutory QR code and unique invoice number, and data is digitally cleared in near real time. There is no separate fiscal clearance stamp, but invoice issuance authority is granted only for already-registered tax codes, and the system automatically reconciles invoice data against VAT returns and customs import/export declarations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the VAT law and implementing regulations, exported goods are zero-rated, provided that the taxpayer is a registered general VAT taxpayer and the goods actually leave Chinese customs territory under an export customs declaration (export declaration), and the foreign exchange received from the export is repatriated and settled in China under foreign exchange regulations. During the construction of deep foundation and diaphragm walls, any exported construction materials, machinery, or equipment permanently supplied to a foreign project may qualify for zero-rating only if they are separately declared as exports and title passes to the overseas buyer. Services provided to overseas recipients for use entirely outside China, including certain international construction services, are zero-rated or VAT-exempt under the 'zero-rated cross-border services' category if the recipient is a foreign entity and the service is delivered and consumed wholly outside mainland China. A WFOE must obtain a general taxpayer status to claim output VAT at 0% and must file the export declaration with the customs authority and the VAT return with the STA, and the refund is processed through the export tax rebate (export VAT refund) system. For deep foundation slurry trenching and diaphragm wall contracting, the service inherently relates to real estate located in China and does not qualify as zero-rated; rather, VAT at 9% applies to the domestic construction service output, while imported equipment and consumables used in China attract import VAT with potential credit. Only goods physically exported from China, such as surplus machinery, tools, or prefabricated materials not installed domestically, may be zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Customs Declaration Form for Exports or Bill of Exit)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / International Throughway Bill for the exported construction equipment or materials
Foreign Exchange Collection and Settlement Confirmation (Bank Receipt/Inward Remittance Certificate showing the export proceeds credited to a Chinese bank account)
Export Invoice issued under China's VAT invoice system with 0% tax rate and export invoice notation
Export Contract and Proforma Invoice evidencing the sale of goods to an overseas purchaser
Proof of export cargo inspection and customs release (Customs Release Certificate) when required for specific controlled goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and customs authorities jointly audit export VAT refund claims and zero-rating documentation. If an export claim is found to be fraudulent, non-qualifying, or improperly documented, the taxpayer must reverse the zero-rating and repay the output VAT, may be denied future refunds, and may face late payment surcharges of 0.05% per day on the underpaid tax. Deliberate fraudulent export tax refunds are subject to criminal liability under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, with penalties of confiscation of illegal gains and imprisonment of up to life imprisonment for amounts above RMB 5,000,000 or with aggravating circumstances. Administrative fines of up to five times the fraudulent refund amount may be imposed, and credit ratings may be downgraded, leading to enhanced scrutiny and mandatory inspection for subsequent refunds. If foreign exchange proceeds are not repatriated and settled within the required 180-day time limit without a valid regulatory extension, the tax authority may deem the export sale as a domestic taxable supply and reassess output VAT at the standard rate plus surcharges and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) together with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), which operates under the PBoC as the exclusive administrative enforcing agency for foreign exchange regulations in the People's Republic of China.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese renminbi (RMB) is fully convertible on the current account following the IMF Article VIII obligations since 1996, meaning trade-related receipts and payments, dividends, interest, and royalties may generally be settled directly through designated foreign exchange banks with genuine transaction documentation. The capital account, however, remains heavily controlled: foreign direct investment (FDI) into a wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) requires prior approval or filing with the Ministry of Commerce and at least a simplified foreign exchange registration with SAFE (via banks under the SAFE FITC system). Capital injected as registered paid-in capital is credited to a foreign exchange capital account (外汇资本金账户) and may be converted into RMB through a bank under the 'Payment-Use' model, strictly for approved business purposes such as procurement of domestic materials, payroll, or land lease, but not for working capital loans, equity investments, or speculative hedging. Settlement of FDI capital requires a domestic investment confirmation and, for amounts exceeding the current account threshold, a non-bank capital account payment instruction. Profit remittance to the foreign shareholder is permitted only after an annual statutory audit, tax clearance certificates, and a board resolution approving the dividend distribution; the bank must verify that the WFOE has completed its corporate income tax withholding on dividends and that the underlying profits were genuinely generated from operational activities and not from currency appreciation or non-operating gains. There is no surrender or conversion quota on current-account transactions, but all outbound remittances exceeding USD 50,000 per transaction require documentary evidence of the underlying transaction and may be subject to further SAFE oversight. The overall regime necessitates a disciplined treasury structure that segregates capital-account inflows, operational RMB accounts, and foreign-currency settlement accounts to ensure full traceability and auditability under SAFE's 'Revision of Measures for the Administration of Foreign Exchange in Direct Investment' and the Personal Information Protection Law cross-border data transfer rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: As of 2012, SAFE removed the mandatory surrender requirement for export proceeds; enterprises are allowed to retain all foreign currency receipts in their export settlement foreign exchange accounts. However, repatriation is mandatory: all export foreign currency receipts must be received into the enterprise's domestic foreign exchange settlement account within 180 days from the date of customs declaration (except where SAFE grants an extended period for bona fide operational reasons). No fixed conversion ratio is imposed; the enterprise may choose to hold the foreign currency or voluntarily convert to RMB at the prevailing market rate at any time. The bank will verify export revenue authenticity through the electronic customs declaration data, logistics bills, and the Enterprise-Individual Foreign Exchange settlement system. Any receipt that cannot be linked to a verified export declaration within the 180-day window may be classified as a capital-account inflow and subjected to additional declaration and approval requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI Capital Account) and Comprehensive Operational RMB Basic Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Settlement Account for Export Proceeds and RMB General Operating Account
Capital Escrow Account and Dedicated Custody Account for Construction Milestone Payments
Basic Deposit Account (Liquidity Concentration) with Multi-currency Sweeping Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) and virtual account providers have essentially zero legal viability as primary banking rails for a China-domiciled WFOE. The PBoC and SAFE require all foreign exchange and RMB capital transactions to be conducted through chartered domestic banks that are connected to the China Foreign Exchange Trade System (CFETS) and subject to SAFE's direct regulatory reporting. International EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, or Payoneer cannot provide a domestic RMB account number or process SAFE-regulated capital inflows; their services are limited to ancillary cross-border payment collection in non-RMB currencies for e-commerce or small-amount trade, and they are legally barred from offering local settlement to Chinese legal entities without a banking license from the CBIRC. The only acceptable use of a foreign EMI is as a pre-funding convenience for the offshore shareholder to aggregate funds before instructing a SWIFT transfer to the WFOE's BOC or ICBC capital account. Any attempt to use an EMI as the WFOE's principal operating account would constitute a breach of the Administrative Measures for the Foreign Exchange Settlement of Capital and violate the renminbi settlement discipline.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the initial opening of a RMB Basic Deposit Account (人民币基本存款账户), the WFOE's statutory legal representative (either a foreign director or the appointed general manager) must appear physically in the bank branch for an on-site KYC interview, as mandated under the PBoC's Account Opening Management Measures and the AML implementation guidelines. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for the basic account because the bank must perform face-to-face verification of the beneficial owner's identity. However, for a foreign legal representative who is physically outside China, the bank may accept a notarized power of attorney issued by the Chinese embassy or consulate in the representative's jurisdiction, coupled with a video interview via the bank's secure teleconference system, but only after the domestic general manager or a jointly-authorized Chinese resident signatory completes the physical branch appearance. For the separate Foreign Exchange Capital Account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account, the same physical presence requirement applies to the designated account signatory, though SAFE allows a fully remote onboarding if the account is opened through the bank's 'Simplify-Connect' digital channel and the legal representative completes a strict video-based four-eyes verification with the bank's compliance officer. In practice, a physical kickoff meeting at the BOC/ICBC headquarters branch is strongly recommended to accelerate the bank's internal risk approval and obtain a higher daily transaction ceiling for the construction sector.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is a foreign legal person registered in a low-tax jurisdiction (e.g., BVI or Cayman) without visible operating substance above the Chinese WFOE, triggering enhanced scrutiny under PBoC's circular on beneficial owner identification and FATF-style transparency expectations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The compliance committee should be presented with: (i) a full set of notarized corporate registry certificates of the UBO and all intermediate holding companies showing a continuous shareholding chain from the ultimate natural persons to the WFOE; (ii) audited financial statements of the intermediate holding companies for the last 3 years demonstrating economic substance (employer records, office leases, and local tax filings); (iii) certified passports of each natural person owning more than 25% of the chain; (iv) a bank reference letter from the UBO's home jurisdiction Tier-1 bank stating KYC performed and no adverse profiles; and (v) a signed sworn declaration that none of the UBOs are politically exposed persons. If a BVI vehicle is unavoidable, add a robust corporate substance certificate issued by the BVI Registry and a tax residency certificate from the BVI International Tax Authority to prove that the vehicle is not a shell.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The WFOE's stated business scope includes deep slurry trenching and diaphragm wall works, which may be flagged under 'construction and infrastructure' as a sector with elevated risk of subcontractor fraud, false invoices, and use of large cash payments for site wages.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit to the bank: (i) the validated statutory business license and the D&B or NCI enterprise credit report; (ii) a pipeline of specific project contracts (in Chinese and English) with known state-owned or private developers, including the project site addresses and contract value; (iii) the company's internal anti-fraud manual and subcontractor onboarding policy proving that all subcontractors are AML-screened and payments are made only through bank transfers; (iv) a detailed cash-flow projection showing that all payroll amounts will be deposited through the banking system with no cash advances; and (v) monthly construction milestone certificates signed by a qualified engineer or third-party supervisor, confirming that each disbursement corresponds to a verified physical event.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The inbound capital injection from the sole foreign shareholder arrives in multiple tranches with mismatched transaction narratives, potentially implying that the funds are shareholder loans rather than registered equity, or that the remitter is not the registered shareholder but a related third-party lender (undisclosed external financing).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the bank with: (i) the board resolution approving each capital call and the updated articles of association reflecting the aggregate paid-in capital schedule; (ii) the SAFE Foreign Investment Registration (FDI Foundation) or the amended Foreign Exchange Business Registration Form showing the exact amount of registered and paid-in capital; (iii) the remittance instruction from the shareholder's bank clearly identifying the shareholder's name and account number matching the registration; (iv) a certified copy of the remitter's board resolution if the funds are injected by a subsidiary of the registered shareholder, together with an assignment of claim or a designated funding notice executed under Chinese law; (v) the capital verification report (验资报告) issued by a licensed Chinese CPA firm within 30 days of the receipt; and (vi) evidence of the source of funds of the remitter (e.g., audited group financial statements, dividend approvals, or SPV loan agreements with a global bank).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The WFOE plans to disburse large outbound payments to foreign equipment suppliers or specialist subcontractors, but the payment purpose codes may indicate a transfer of technology or service fees, which are subject to withholding tax and SAFE scrutiny, potentially triggering an automatic compliance hold on the corporate account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The compliance package must include: (i) the executed export sales or equipment lease agreement covering the specific machinery for trench cutters and slurry wall clamps, with a clear breakdown of lease versus purchase value; (ii) the customs import declaration and bill of lading for any physical equipment crossing the border; (iii) the invoice and the bank's own tax advice confirming that any withholding tax on royalties/services has been settled with the tax bureau; (iv) a technology import contract registration certificate issued by the provincial commerce authority if any proprietary know-how is involved; and (v) a legal opinion from a Chinese law firm confirming that the payment purpose code (e.g., 321-As per contract or 324-Operating lease) is correctly matched and that the transaction is not a disguised dividend or capital flight.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the WFOE to lawfully receive foreign equity capital: (1) the foreign shareholder must first complete the SAFE direct investment registration at the local SAFE office or through a designated bank (bank-led registration) using the Foreign Investment Registration form; (2) the WFOE must open a dedicated Foreign Exchange Capital Account (外汇资本金账户) at a Tier-1 bank such as BOC or ICBC, with the bank's business license and the SAFE registration code; (3) the offshore remittance must be a clean SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for a bank-to-bank transfer) from the registered shareholder's bank account to the WFOE's capital account, with the remittance field explicitly indicating 'Investment Capital' and including the country code 'CN' and the Chinese entity name; (4) the payment purpose code according to SAFE's 'Code for International Transactions' should be '621-Investor's capital injection' or '622-Investment in a foreign-invested enterprise' — the bank will validate this code against the registration; (5) upon receipt, the bank credits the foreign exchange capital account and the WFOE must provide a capital verification report issued by a Chinese CPA within 30 days, confirming the paid-in capital; (6) for RMB settlement of the capital account, the WFOE completes the 'Payment-Use' conversion (资本金结汇) by submitting a determination letter, a valid underlying invoice or contract, and a completed 'Capital Account Payment Confirmation Form' to the bank; the bank will credit the RMB funds to the WFOE's operating RMB account under a dedicated RMB account 'settlement code' — no conversion is allowed for speculative inventory or real estate investments; (7) all inbound capital transactions must be reported to SAFE through the bank's ASONE system within 1 business day. A shareholder loan (外债) injection is possible only under the macro-prudential foreign debt cap (outstanding foreign debt capped at 2x of net assets), and requires a separate SAFE foreign debt registration, a contractual loan agreement, and must be settled under a 'Foreign Loan' purpose code; failure to follow this route would result in a serious AML sandbox violation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the WFOE's milestone-based business as a geotechnical contractor, outbound cash flows will primarily be (a) domestic RMB payments to subcontractors, suppliers, and workers, routed through the company's RMB basic account using a Corporate Banking internet system with MT103-equivalent domestic transfer messages (PBoC's HVPS or CNAPS) — each payment must reference the project contract and the actual milestone invoice, and must not exceed the project's budgeted cost block without an updated board approval; (b) cross-border outbound payments for imported equipment, overseas rental of diaphragm wall grabs, and specialist consulting, routed via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign exchange settlement account, with a bank-coded purpose (e.g., '321-Operating lease payment' or '324-Purchase of capital equipment') and supporting documents (import contract, proforma invoice, customs declaration, and legally approved tax certificates). If the WFOE or its parent company is selling services or renting equipment to the Chinese project entity, the cross-border transaction must be an arm's-length contract with a tax invoice and transfer-pricing documentation to withstand challenge from the State Taxation Administration. For larger project settlements exceeding USD 200,000, the bank will offer a Documentary Collection (DC) against shipping documents (B/L, insurance, commercial invoice, packing list) or a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) issued by a Chinese bank as an independent undertaking for payments to the subcontractor or supplier; the LC route is strongly recommended for any overseas equipment or pro-foreign subcontractor payment above USD 500,000 to mitigate counterparty risk and ensure compliance with SAFE's 'real need' doctrine. All outbound payments require the WFOE to have a valid transaction folder that is retained for at least 5 years and available for SAFE spot-check.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/USD forward contracts (settled onshore, with confirmed underlying trade exposure and board-approved hedging memorandum) — permitted only for genuine current-account transactions and not for speculative trading.

RMB foreign exchange swaps (fix-to-floating or floating-to-fixing) with a licensed domestic bank for hedging the interest rate or currency basis between RMB and USD, subject to SAFE's real-need documentation.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) on foreign currency debt or project finance, entered under a CSA (Credit Support Annex) with an eligible PRC bank counterparty, provided the notional principal matches the underlying foreign debt payable.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on RMB are not permitted onshore for Chinese domestic legal entities; undertakings in offshore CNH NDFs or options are strictly prohibited for state-owned-enterprise-linked WFOEs without SAFE special approval, and therefore should be avoided. Onshore options on spot FX with a zero-cost collar structure may be used where the bank has an underlying corporate demand and the transaction is reported to SAFE as a financial derivative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Report and Foreign Investment Information Annual Report (combined E-Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, with controlled data sharing to the Ministry of Commerce for foreign investment statistics
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June immediately following the reporting fiscal year; no anniversary extension for offshore groups
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing by 30 June places the WFOE on the public 'abnormal operations' list within 10 working days; each year of default extends the abnormal listing. If unresolved for three consecutive years, SAMR upgrades the company to the 'serious illegal and untrustworthy enterprises' list, triggering cross-agency credit bans, procurement disqualifications, enhanced audit scrutiny, and eventual administrative deregistration or business license revocation where the company remains non-operational.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement Return and Final Payment (annual CIT reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local tax service bureau of the State Taxation Administration (STA) in the WFOE's tax registration jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the year immediately following the tax year, with quarterly prepayments due by 15 April, 15 July, 15 October and 15 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment triggers a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax from the statutory due date, plus administrative fines under the PRC Tax Administration Law. Continued default may lead to bank account freezing, forced asset attachment, tax assessment by estimation, suspension of business license, administrative revocation, and criminal referral for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Financial Audit Report prepared by an independent CICPA-registered accounting firm and delivered to shareholders/board
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation and State Taxation Administration (available for inspection and audit enforcement; no routine standing government receipt)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual financial statements must be prepared at fiscal year-end and the audit completed before the annual shareholders' meeting; typical market practice requires finalization by 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to have annual financial statements audited under PRC Company Law exposes directors and supervisors to civil and administrative liability. In tax audits, defective or unaudited accounting records can trigger penalty assessments of 5% to 100% of underpaid tax and mandatory record reconstruction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual register inspection readiness, tax record retention, and statutory books of account upkeep for WFOE corporate records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation, local SAMR authorities, and State Taxation Administration during on-site register audits and tax investigations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Retention period is at least 7 years; inspection-readiness is continuous and year-round without a separate annual filing in a quiet fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing books and vouchers, incomplete registers, or failure to produce records on demand are penalized under PRC Tax Administration Law and company-registration regulations; persistent noncompliance can trigger compulsory audit, qualification disqualification for construction licensees, administrative revocation, or deregistration of the WFOE.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a PRC WFOE the independent audit requirements are effectively universal; the quantitative trigger is zero balance sheet, zero turnover, and zero headcount exemption. PRC Company Law (Article 164 of the 2018 version, with the obligation substantively retained under current PRC company legislation) provides that every company must prepare annual financial reports and have them audited by a lawfully constituted accounting firm. In addition, the SAMR annual report system and the foreign investment information reporting system require certified financial data, and construction enterprises under the deep foundation/diaphragm wall contracting scope face mandatory audit or certified financial statements as part of construction qualification and safety production license maintenance. No safe-harbour revenue, asset, or employee threshold removes a WFOE from the statutory audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CASBE, substantially IFRS-converged) as the primary statutory accounting framework for WFOEs that use full standards; qualifying small enterprises may apply the 2013 Small Enterprise Accounting Standards (CAS-SEAS) where legally eligible, with full CASBE required for any listed/publicly issued entity or where comprehensive standards are adopted. Financial statements are prepared and presented in RMB with English translation in cross-border corporate practice.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China does not maintain a separate annual UBO return for ordinary WFOEs; beneficial-owner and actual-controller information is confirmed through the combined SAMR Enterprise Annual Report and Foreign Investment Information Annual Report filed by 30 June each year, and the filing must confirm the shareholding percentages, paid-in capital, actual controllers and foreign ownership details as of 31 December. During the year, any shareholding transfer or change of actual controller must be registered with SAMR within 30 days from the date the change occurs. Failure to register the change leaves it unenforceable against third parties and subjects the transferring parties to administrative penalties; for licensed construction WFOEs, a shareholding transfer or actual-controller change also requires coordination with the construction qualification regulator.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 2,500 per annum (registered address plus corporate secretarial agent services in tier-1/tier-2 Chinese cities); higher where legal representative services or construction-labor registration support are included
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 8,000 per annum for a mid-sized deep foundation/diaphragm wall construction WFOE, depending on turnover, related-party transactions, intercompany balances, and CASBE complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: China applies a 25% headline Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) rate. A WFOE engaged in deep slurry trenching and underground continuous cut-off wall works may, if it qualifies as a Small Low-Profit Enterprise with taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million, obtain an effective 5% rate for the qualifying portion (statutory 20% rate applied to a reduced 25% portion of income). Qualified R&D expenses are eligible for a 100% additional deduction. No automatic free-zone tax holiday applies to the WFOE merely by virtue of foreign ownership; any preferential 15% West Region development rate is available only if the enterprise is located in a qualifying western region and operates in an encouraged industry. Loss carryforward is five years for standard enterprises and ten years for qualifying high-tech or technology-advanced small- and medium-sized enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return Form A (A100000 main return, together with supporting schedules such as A105000 Tax Adjustment Item Schedule, A107010 Preferential Tax Rate Schedule, and A108000 Foreign Tax Credit Schedule) for the 2017 revision series. Filing is made through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal (eTax / e-Tax platform) or directly with the competent Chinese tax authority where the WFOE is tax registered.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement with quarterly provisional prepayments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional EIT prepayment returns are due within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter. The annual Form A tax return and final settlement must be filed within five calendar months after the tax year-end, i.e., on or before May 31 of the following year. The tax year is the Gregorian calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name of the WFOE, Unified Social Credit Code, address, tax registration number, and registered capital.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact USCC matching the Foreign-Invested Enterprise business license. Non-resident shareholders must be identified by country of residence in the supplementary shareholder information; failure to state treaty jurisdiction may impede later DTA claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Return type indicator: ordinary annual return, amended return, or refund/final settlement declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark the annual settlement return. If the WFOE has received notices from tax authorities regarding related-party transactions or transfer pricing audits, indicate the amended-return status and attach explanations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting basis and financial statement currency: accrual basis, calendar year, RMB functional currency.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use RMB as the reporting currency. If foreign currency books have been maintained, convert income and deductible expenses at the annually announced average exchange rate or transaction-date rate consistently with tax rules. The percentage-of-completion method is commonly required for long-term construction contracts such as deep diaphragm wall works.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue from principal operations: gross receipts from deep slurry trenching, diaphragm wall construction, geotechnical foundation contracting, and related construction services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report revenue exclusive of VAT output tax. Construction milestone revenue must match contract progress certificates. If the WFOE contracts with a non-resident related party, document that the intercompany price has been set at arm's length and that no artificial deferral of revenue has occurred.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of principal operations: direct job costs, subcontractor fees, materials, bentonite and slurry consumables, labor costs, machinery depreciation, and equipment mobilization costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All costs must be supported by compliant fapiao or equivalent tax invoices. Payments to non-resident subcontractors or equipment providers must be supported by withholding tax evidence; unsubstantiated cross-border service payments are non-deductible and may trigger transfer pricing adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit or gross loss from principal operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compare gross margin with independent construction contractors performing comparable foundation works. A materially lower gross margin relative to the arm's-length range will attract scrutiny for transfer pricing recharacterization and profit attribution to the Chinese permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses, administrative expenses, and finance expenses; including R&D additional deduction, employee compensation, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border management fees, headquarters charges, and technical assistance fees paid to the overseas parent, deductibility requires an actual service contract, evidence of service delivery, arm's-length pricing, and remittance of non-resident withholding tax. General allocations without real services are non-deductible. Entertainment expenses are limited under the lower of 60% and 5 per mille of sales; advertising expenses are subject to caps.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment items: add-back of non-deductible expenditures and reverse of tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fines, late surcharges, penalties, bribery-related payments, unlawful compensation, and invoices issued by shell entities must be added back. Also add back non-resident taxes borne by the WFOE on behalf of the parent unless treaty or law permits otherwise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss carryforward and adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim loss carryforward only within the statutory period; the standard five-year carryforward applies to the WFOE unless it qualifies as a high-tech enterprise. Losses generated in foreign branches are not available to offset Chinese-source taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of EIT: taxable income multiplied by tax rate, less foreign tax credits, less quarterly prepayments, equals final tax payable or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply either 25% standard rate or the reduced effective rate if qualified as a Small Low-Profit Enterprise. Attach Schedule A108000 for foreign tax credit positions. If the WFOE has a foreign parent, no consolidation or group relief is allowed at the Chinese entity level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 / Line 11 (Schedule for profit distribution to non-resident investors)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: After-tax retained earnings available for distribution, dividend resolutions in favor of non-resident shareholders, and WHT calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend withholding is triggered at the time of distribution or deemed distribution to a non-resident enterprise. Report the amount distributed, the statutory 10% WHT, and any treaty-reduced rate only where a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership statement are on file with the WFOE. Failure to withhold creates primary liability for the WFOE as withholding agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual EIT return triggers a fine under Article 62 of the Law on Tax Administration and Tax Collection (TAL) of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, increasing to RMB 2,000 to RMB 20,000 for severe cases. Late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of unpaid tax. A false or fraudulent return causing underpayment of tax is addressed by TAL Article 63: confiscation of the evaded tax plus a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount. Where tax evasion exceeds RMB 50,000 and constitutes more than 10% of the amount of tax payable, criminal liability may arise under PRC Criminal Law Article 201, with imprisonment of up to three years for relatively large amounts and up to seven years for huge amounts, together with fines. Major tax violations are published by the State Taxation Administration, resulting in joint disciplinary blacklisting, travel restrictions, and credit impairment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10%: Dividends paid by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise shareholder are subject to Enterprise Income Tax withheld at source at 10% under EIT Law Article 37 and the implementing regulations. No withholding is required for distributions to Chinese resident corporate shareholders; treaty relief may reduce the rate to 5% or other applicable rates only after proper qualification.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim bilateral Double Tax Treaty (DTA) relief on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties, the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the WFOE and the Chinese tax authority: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority for the relevant fiscal year, certifying residence in the treaty jurisdiction; (2) a signed Beneficial Owner Declaration confirming the recipient is the substantive beneficial owner with control and economic substance, not an agent or conduit; (3) documentary evidence of shareholding percentage and holding period when a reduced 5% dividend rate depends on 25% or higher ownership for the minimum required period; and (4) completed non-resident withholding return and treaty benefit application through the e-tax platform or Form based on State Taxation Administration Announcement No. 60 of 2015. The WFOE must withhold the statutory 10% rate unless the treaty relief is properly substantiated; where documentation is deficient, the statutory rate applies. Any under-withholding is recoverable from the WFOE as withholding agent, including late surcharges and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on outbound interest, royalties, rental income, and other passive income paid to non-resident enterprises is 10%. Many Chinese DTAs provide for a 10% or reduced rate; for example, payments to Hong Kong or Singapore residents frequently attract 7% interest and royalty rates or 5% where beneficial ownership and licensing substance tests are met. Royalties for technical know-how, patents, software, and industrial processes may be taxed at the same 10% statutory rate or at treaty-reduced rates. The WFOE must file the Non-Resident Enterprise Income Tax Withholding Return within the prescribed period, remit the withheld tax, and provide the payee with a certificate of tax withholding for its foreign tax credit.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42, a Chinese enterprise must prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File) for related-party transactions exceeding: RMB 200 million for tangible asset transfers; RMB 100 million for intangible asset transfers; RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers; RMB 40 million for related-party service transactions. A Master File is due where the multinational group's combined revenue is RMB 2 billion or above and a Country-by-Country Report is required where group consolidated revenue is RMB 5.5 billion or above. For the WFOE, all intercompany construction, machinery rental, know-how, and management service transactions must be benchmarked under the arm's-length standard.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies substance-over-form through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) in Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and the Special Tax Adjustment rules, rather than a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime. For a WFOE performing ISIC 4390 deep slurry trenching and underground continuous cut-off wall works, the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) must be genuinely performed by the WFOE: project bidding, geotechnical site assessment, slurry mixing and circulation, diaphragm wall excavation, reinforcement installation, concrete pouring, quality inspection, safety supervision, equipment ownership or leasing, and invoicing. If the WFOE lacks employees, management, physical premises, equipment, or risk-bearing capacity, tax authorities may recharacterize income, deny treaty benefits, impose transfer pricing adjustments, and assess penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by False Invoicing and Inflated Project Costs
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors or senior finance managers procure false or retroactive fapiao from shell subcontractors to inflate the cost of deep slurry trenching and diaphragm wall works, understate taxable income, and fraudulently obtain refunds or reduce EIT liabilities. Cash recycling through unregistered subcontractors or fake machinery rental contracts also triggers this violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 63 of the Law on Tax Administration and Tax Collection (TAL), the taxpayer is ordered to pay the underpaid tax within a prescribed period, plus a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount, and daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of unpaid tax. Under PRC Criminal Law Article 201, tax evasion above RMB 50,000 constituting more than 10% of payable tax is criminal tax fraud; Article 205 imposes punishment for issuing false special VAT invoices, including sentences up to life imprisonment for extraordinarily large amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil can be pierced under PRC Company Law where abuse of corporate limited liability fraudulently harms creditors or state tax revenue. Directors who organize false invoicing face personal civil restitution for the tax loss, asset freezing, travel bans and exit-control restrictions, inclusion on the serious tax violation blacklist with consequences for visas and business licenses, criminal imprisonment up to seven years for aggravated evasion, and disqualification from serving as directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Treaty Abuse on Outbound Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE distributes dividends to a Hong Kong or offshore parent without withholding the statutory 10% EIT, or claims a 5% reduced DTA rate through a nominee shareholder lacking beneficial ownership, using an improperly obtained Tax Residency Certificate or fabricated substance. Related misuse includes converting dividends into deductible interest or royalties without economic reality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under TAL Article 69, a withholding agent that fails to collect or remit withholding tax is subject to a penalty of 50% to 300% of the uncollected tax, plus the taxpayer remains liable for the tax. Under Article 47 of the EIT Law, the GAAR may disregard the treaty arrangement, recharacterize the shareholder as non-eligible, and assess the full 10% WHT with late surcharges. The unilateral declaration of treaty benefits without supporting TRC and beneficial ownership documentation is an administrative violation and may be treated as tax fraud in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve unlawful distributions or sign false treaty applications expose themselves to personal joint liability for the unremitted tax where company assets are stripped or the company becomes insolvent. Civil asset restitution may be ordered, travel bans and blacklisting under the joint disciplinary mechanism apply for unpaid taxes, and criminal liability can arise for intentional withholding tax evasion, including imprisonment up to seven years and fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Structure and Fake Economic Substance with Fraudulent Preferential Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE operates as a paper conduit with no geotechnical staff, no diaphragm wall equipment, no slurry management capability, no project site, and no decision-making authority; it artificially splits contracts among affiliated shell entities to keep each entity's taxable income below RMB 3 million to obtain the 5% Small Low-Profit Enterprise rate, or routes all profit to offshore services that are never performed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under EIT Law Article 47 and SAT Special Tax Adjustment rules, the tax authority may recharacterize the entire arrangement, attribute income to the entity performing real functions and risks, deny the Small Low-Profit preferential rate, and impose a tax shortfall with late surcharge. TAL Article 63 imposes a 50% to 500% fine for false returns. False preferential tax claims also trigger administrative blacklisting and multi-department joint punishment, including suspension of qualification for government construction tenders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil under PRC Company Law when shareholders use the limited liability entity to evade tax obligations, causing directors who are also shareholders to bear unlimited joint liability. Directors signing false substance certificates or tax preferences are personally liable for restitution of tax benefits, subject to asset seizure, blacklisting, exit bans under enforcement measures, and criminal liability for fraud if the false claims exceed criminal thresholds. In geotechnical contracting, the absence of licensed professional engineers on site can also lead to revocation of safety and construction licenses and personal criminal liability for workplace safety incidents.
